# `modernize-reify-type`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: modernize · Default: off · Fixes: fix all · Options: none

Reports `@Type` calls, which Zig 0.16 replaced with `@Int`, `@Struct`, `@Tuple`,
`@Union`, `@Enum`, `@Pointer`, `@Fn` and `@EnumLiteral`, rewriting integer,
enum-literal and primitive reifications.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Zig 0.16 removed `@Type`; a call to it no longer compiles. Each kind of type
it built now has its own builtin taking the parts as arguments: `@Int(signedness,
bits)`, `@Struct(layout, BackingInt, field_names, field_types, field_attrs)`,
`@Tuple(field_types)`, `@Union(layout, ArgType, field_names, field_types,
field_attrs)`, `@Enum(TagInt, mode, field_names, field_values)`,
`@Pointer(size, attrs, Element, sentinel)`, `@Fn(param_types, param_attrs,
ReturnType, attrs)` and `@EnumLiteral()`. Floats, arrays, optionals, error
unions and opaque types use their type syntax, and error sets can no longer be
reified.

## When it fires

On every `@Type(...)` call. The message names the replacement for the kind the
argument literal selects (`.{ .int = ... }`, `.{ .@"struct" = ... }`, ...), or
lists the builtins when the argument is not a literal. Three shapes are
rewritten, also by `check --fix`, because the replacement is the same type:
`@Type(.{ .int = .{ .signedness = s, .bits = b } })` becomes `@Int(s, b)` (the
two fields in either order, each expression kept as written),
`@Type(.enum_literal)` becomes `@EnumLiteral()`, and `@Type(.bool)` and the
other payload-free primitive tags become the primitive type. A call containing
a comment keeps it and gets no fix.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const Byte = @Type(.{ .int = .{ .signedness = .unsigned, .bits = 8 } });
```

Reference: <https://ziglang.org/download/0.16.0/release-notes.html>
